title: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing fractions
blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers by hand, the way the TEAS calculator can't.
question: A hospital kitchen has 5 1/3 cups of oats, and each batch of oatmeal uses 2/3 cup. How many batches can be made, and which operation gets you there?

teach.body: Formally, fractions can be added or subtracted only when they share a common denominator; multiplication and division need no common denominator. In plain English: to add or subtract, first cut everything into same-size pieces; to multiply, multiply straight across; to divide, flip the second fraction and multiply. The TEAS calculator has no fraction key, so you must do these by hand.

teach.h: The four operations side by side
teach.caption: Always simplify the final answer.

items: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of 3 and 4: 12.
Add the numerators, keep the denominator: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.
Write as a mixed number: 17 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 5, so 1 5/12.
The fraction 1/4 is smaller than 3/4, so borrow 1 whole from the 5.
Check by improper fractions: 21/4 − 11/4 = 10/4 = 2 1/2. ✓
Convert both mixed numbers: 2 1/2 = 5/2 and 1 3/5 = 8/5.
Cross-cancel: the 5 on top and the 5 on the bottom cancel, leaving 1/2 × 8/1.
Multiply: 1 × 8 = 8 and 2 × 1 = 2, so 8/2 = 4.
Check with decimals: 2.5 × 1.6 = 4. ✓

teach.caption: Only the second fraction (the divisor) flips. Check: 2/3 × 9/8 = 18/24 = 3/4. ✓

head: Denominators
Multiples of the larger
LCD
teach.caption: List multiples of the larger denominator until the smaller one divides in evenly.

teach.text: Three classic slips: adding the denominators (1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7 is wrong; it is 7/12); flipping the wrong fraction, or both, when dividing; and multiplying a mixed number without converting it (2 1/2 × 4 is 10, not 8 1/2).

teach.body: Priya Patel, a nursing applicant working in a hospital kitchen, has 5 1/3 cups of oats and each batch needs 2/3 cup. "How many 2/3s fit in 5 1/3?" means divide. 5 1/3 = 16/3. Keep, change, flip: 16/3 × 3/2 = 48/6 = 8. Check: 8 × 2/3 = 16/3 = 5 1/3. ✓ She can make 8 batches.

items: Add/subtract: common denominator first, then combine numerators only.
Borrow 1 whole as a full fraction (4/4, 6/6...) when the fraction you subtract is bigger.
Multiply: convert mixed numbers, cross-cancel, multiply straight across.
Divide: keep the first, change ÷ to ×, flip the second.
Simplify the answer and check it with decimals or the inverse operation.

summary: You can now add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers by hand, including borrowing and cross-canceling. You know which operation needs a common denominator and which slips the TEAS turns into wrong answers.

A.q: A nurse has 5/6 liter of solution and uses 3/8 liter. How much solution is left?

whyNot.0: 29/24 adds the fractions (20 + 9) instead of subtracting.
whyNot.1: 1/12 = 2/24 changes the denominators to 24 but leaves the numerators as 5 and 3.
whyNot.3: 11/48 uses the right numerator (11, from twenty-fourths) over the wrong denominator, 48.

A.q: A recipe uses 3/4 cup of milk per batch. How much milk is needed for 2 1/2 batches?
A.why: Convert: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Then 3/4 × 5/2 = 15/8 = 1 7/8 cups. Check: 2 batches use 1 1/2 cups and half a batch uses 3/8 cup; 1 4/8 + 3/8 = 1 7/8.

whyNot.0: 2 3/8 multiplies only the 1/2 by 3/4 (3/8) and keeps the 2, instead of converting 2 1/2 first.
whyNot.1: 3 1/4 adds 3/4 and 2 1/2; "per batch" for several batches calls for multiplying.
whyNot.2: 1 1/2 is the milk for 2 batches only; the half batch is missing.

A.q: A bottle holds 12 tablespoons of liquid antacid. Each dose is 3/4 tablespoon. How many doses are in the bottle?

whyNot.0: 9 is 12 × 3/4: it multiplies by the dose instead of dividing by it.
whyNot.2: 36 multiplies by the numerator 3 instead of by the flipped fraction 4/3.
whyNot.3: 48 multiplies by 4 but forgets to divide by 3.

B.q: A patient drank 1 2/3 cups of water at breakfast and 2 3/4 cups at lunch. How much did the patient drink in total?

whyNot.0: 3 5/7 adds the numerators and the denominators: (2 + 3)/(3 + 4).
whyNot.1: 3 1/2 multiplies the fraction parts (2/3 × 3/4 = 1/2) instead of adding them.
whyNot.3: 3 5/12 drops the whole 1 inside 17/12 instead of carrying it to the 3.

B.q: A roll had 6 1/3 yards of medical tape, and 2 5/6 yards were used. How much tape is left?

whyNot.0: 4 1/2 subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger (5/6 − 2/6) instead of borrowing.
whyNot.1: 3 1/3 borrows without first renaming 1/3 as 2/6, so it starts from 5 7/6.
whyNot.2: 9 1/6 adds the two lengths instead of subtracting.

B.q: Which expression has the same value as 4/9 ÷ 2/3?
B.why: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the divisor: 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3.

whyNot.1: This flips the first fraction (the dividend) instead of the divisor.
whyNot.2: This flips both fractions; only the divisor flips.
whyNot.3: This changes ÷ to × without flipping anything, which multiplies instead of divides.

C.q: Each batch of bran muffins uses 2 1/4 cups of flour. How much flour is needed for 2 2/3 batches?
C.why: Convert: 2 1/4 = 9/4 and 2 2/3 = 8/3. Multiply: 9/4 × 8/3 = 72/12 = 6 cups. Cross-cancel check: (3/1) × (2/1) = 6.

whyNot.1: 4 1/6 multiplies the wholes (2 × 2) and the fractions (1/4 × 2/3) separately; mixed numbers must be converted first.
whyNot.2: 4 11/12 adds the two mixed numbers instead of multiplying.
whyNot.3: 27/32 divides 9/4 by 8/3; "per batch" for several batches calls for multiplying.

C.q: Keisha walked 3/4 mile in the morning and 1/6 mile at lunch. Her daily goal is 1 5/6 miles. What fraction of her goal has she walked?

whyNot.0: 11/12 is the distance walked, an intermediate step; it still has to be divided by the goal.
whyNot.2: 2 divides the goal by the distance walked, the division upside down.
whyNot.3: 12/55 comes from adding tops and bottoms (4/10 = 2/5) before dividing by 11/6.

whyNot.0: 6 ÷ 1/2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a larger number; 3 is 6 × 1/2.
whyNot.3: 1/2 × 2 1/2 = 1/2 × 5/2 = 5/4 = 1 1/4; 1 1/2 comes from multiplying only the whole number.

reteach.title: Fractions are like coins
reteach.question: You can't add 1 quarter and 1 dime by saying "2 coins." What do you do first, and how does that explain common denominators?

blocks.body: A quarter is 1/4 of a dollar and a dime is 1/10 of a dollar. To add them you change both to cents, a common unit: 25 + 10 = 35 cents = 35/100 = 7/20 of a dollar. That is exactly what a common denominator does. Multiplying and dividing are different: "how many quarters are in $3?" is 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4 = 12, no common unit needed.

items: How many quarters in $3? 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4/1 = 12 quarters.
How many 3/4-cup scoops in 6 cups? 6 ÷ 3/4 = 6 × 4/3 = 8 scoops.
Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger answer, because many small pieces fit.

blocks.text: 1 quarter + 1 dime is not 2/14 of a dollar. Adding the denominators is like saying two coins are always worth the same.

explain.body: Find the LCD, rename each fraction, then add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. 3/10 + 1/4: LCD 20, so 6/20 + 5/20 = 11/20.

test.q: A patient drinks 3/10 liter of juice and then 1/4 liter of water. How much has the patient drunk in total?

whyNot.0: 4/14 adds the numerators and the denominators.
whyNot.1: 11/40 puts the twentieths numerator over 40; in fortieths the sum is 22/40.
whyNot.2: 3/40 multiplies the fractions instead of adding them.

explain.body: If the fraction you subtract is larger, borrow 1 whole from the whole number and add it as a full fraction (5/5, 6/6...) to the fraction part. 4 1/5 becomes 3 6/5.

test.q: A bag of potting soil weighed 4 1/5 pounds, and 1 3/5 pounds were used. How much is left?

whyNot.0: 3 2/5 subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger (3/5 − 1/5) instead of borrowing.
whyNot.2: 2 2/5 borrows 1 as 5/5 but forgets to add the original 1/5 (3 5/5 instead of 3 6/5).
whyNot.3: 5 4/5 adds the two amounts instead of subtracting.

explain.body: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions, cancel any top with any bottom that share a factor, then multiply straight across. No common denominator needed.

whyNot.0: 1 1/8 multiplies only the fraction part (1/3 × 3/8 = 1/8) and keeps the whole 1.
whyNot.1: 32/9 is 4/3 × 8/3: it flips the second fraction, which is division.
whyNot.3: 7/11 adds the numerators and denominators of 4/3 and 3/8.

explain.body: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the second (the divisor). Only the divisor flips. 5/6 ÷ 2/3 = 5/6 × 3/2.

whyNot.2: 4/5 flips the first fraction instead of the divisor: 6/5 × 2/3.
